text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak says the efforts of the nation are aimed at setting up grandscale development projects that have no precedent in history. The main aim is to increase the rate of development until it is three times the population growth rate. We want to realise the Arab common market project so we can have a correct start to creating the Arab economy.

- Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri issues a decree aimed at curtailing government spending. Ministries and civil services are not allowed to set up new funds, buy new passenger cars or hook up new telephone lines. Decree also bans purchase of any new furniture, expect for hospital use.

- Privatisation committee approves a programme to restructure 55 public firms in the food, chemical, refraction and metals insdustries. The programme aims at achieving a seven to 10 percent revenue in these firms within six months.
- Suez Canal revenues amounted to $1 billion in 1996.
- Mubarak says in a speech commemorating the anniversary of the July 23, 1952 revolution: The revolution caused a historic volte face in the Middle East and changed the philosophy of governance.
- Interior Minister Hassan el-Alfi approves latest personnel changes in the police force.
- Libyan leader Muammar Gaddafi: Mubarak has made a lot of achievements for the Egyptian people.
- Egypt gets three more gold medals in Arab Games
- Israeli Knesset issues a new law banning the withdrawal from the Golan Heights.
- King Fahd of Saudi Arabia telephones Mubarak.
- Number of farmers that will be affected by the new land ownership law has fallen to 10 percent of the total.
